episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 4, 2026
episodes.summary: The last few days on this beat were about OpenAI's DevDay products. Today turns to two launches this show has not touched yet, one from Google and one from IBM, plus a rollout from Anthropic. A quick sourcing note. The Google pricing and access terms come from Google's own release post.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon lifts the output ceiling of a single agent run to one million tokens, and Google has already said its introductory price will double.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 4, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. It is Sunday, and no market has closed since Friday. So my calls on rates, Bitcoin, oil, gold, uranium and the Fed carry over exactly as they stood yesterday. The Brent call stays a provisional hit. It is still waiting on a verified close below a hundred dollars.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Friday's jobs report is three days old, and the argument over what it did to the Fed path is still running. That argument matters less than it looks. The reason why is today's story.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Last week on this beat belonged to OpenAI's DevDay headliners and Google's Gemini 4 Argon. Today is about smaller pieces: a call that makes a decision, a coding tool that operates the desktop, and voice priced for volume. A sourcing note before we start.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this beat has counted humanoid robots. Now the industry has started putting prices and payback periods on them. Neither one is a delivery, and that distinction is the story this morning.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Two recent developments show where defense-space money is concentrating and where it is still contested. The first is the National Reconnaissance Office's first-ever launch on a Falcon Heavy. The second is a 369-million-dollar Space Development Agency solicitation for missile-tracking ground stations.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: The tender result we have been waiting on is in, and it does not say what we expected. Blue Owl again limited withdrawals to 5% at two of its private credit vehicles. But the two vehicles moved in opposite directions. That is a queue sorting by sector, not a queue draining.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: investors in Blue Owl's technology-focused credit vehicle reportedly asked to redeem 39 percent of its shares against a 5 percent cap, even as requests at the firm's flagship fund eased.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 5, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and with a grade I owe. I had called for redemption requests at Blue Owl's flagship retail credit fund, Blue Owl Credit Income Corp, to match or beat last quarter's. I gave it one-in-three. Today's private credit read has requests falling, from 18.8 percent of shares to 16.8.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with the long end. On Treasury's daily par yield curve, the ten-year closed Monday at 5.31 percent. That is up from 5.24 percent on October first. It is the highest ten-year close this desk has tracked in this selloff, and the thirty-year rose with it.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Today is two deals, and both make the same bet. Durable value in enterprise software sits in the system of record that AI and agents write into. In both cases, the bull case rests on the hardest number to deliver.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Two corrections open today's briefing, and they point in opposite directions. On Saturday we told you Google's Gemini 4 Argon was priced at half of Claude Opus 5.5, and that this put pressure on Anthropic's flagship tier. We also told you the open-weight counterweight from China had gone untested.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: The lead today is Bitcoin, and the question this desk has carried since late September: who is actually the marginal buyer? This week's answer is not the one the narrative prefers.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis is simple. The oil chain is being fought over by force again, at the Strait of Hormuz and inside Russia's refineries.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Last week on this beat was about what OpenAI shipped at its DevDay conference. Today is about something different: how those agents reach buyers, and who ends up paying for them.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: The thread this week is money. Capital for physical AI is moving off venture term sheets and onto corporate balance sheets. A chipmaker agreed to pay in stock for a world-model lab, and Tesla lined up bank credit.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline today is a small number with a large implication. Bloomberg reports that KKR's retail credit fund, K-FITS, received repurchase requests for 5.06 percent of its shares in the tender that expired September 29th. The fund said it would buy back every share tendered.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: The two biggest chip stories since our last briefing are really the same story. Both are about who pays for the capacity. In one, the chip supplier is putting up the money. In the other, the customer is. That difference tells you a lot about where bargaining power sits right now.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: The thesis today is that the private equity liquidity problem is moving. It started in the exit window. It is now showing up in the wealth channel, where the promise of semi-liquid access meets a distribution drought.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: the ten-year Treasury closed Monday at 5.31 percent, and the two-year rose right along with it, which Capital Markets Radar reads as the market pricing a tighter Fed rather than just heavier bond supply.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 6, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, and with a call going against me. On Saturday I said Bitcoin records no daily close above eighty-five thousand dollars before September CPI on October 14th, at fifty-five percent. Today's digital money read has Bitcoin near eighty-six thousand two hundred on October 5th.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's open question was whether China's open-weight counterweight would actually show up. On Saturday we said it had gone untested. Yesterday we corrected that, and said DeepSeek's open weights set a floor under the mid-tier on price. Today the same floor-setter shows up with capital.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: On Monday, the ten-year Treasury touched its highest level since April 2002. By Tuesday's close, the S&P 500 had set its 28th record close of the year, and the Nasdaq Composite had notched another record of its own. Today's question is how both things are true at once.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis. The institutional layer of digital assets is sitting at breakeven, not expanding. Bitcoin is pinned near the price where its largest holders get their money back. The on-chain dollar stack has stopped growing, even as its usage falls.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis has three parts. Real new megawatts are starting to show up, but in small increments and on slow timelines. The demand claims behind the AI buildout are finally being audited.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Let's start with memory, because this week it got a number. Korean press reports say Samsung is seeking more than three times its current HBM3E price for next-generation HBM4. Samsung reportedly proposed a price in the mid-to-high four dollar range per gigabit for 2027. HBM3E sits at roughly one and a half dollars.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Before we start, a disclosure. Anthropic makes the model behind this show, and today's lead story is an Anthropic product. Weigh what follows with that in mind.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's question is where control sits in enterprise software. The control point is moving above the individual application. Nobody has yet shown that customers will pay for that new layer.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the builder. On Thursday, October 1, this show led with Roche's investor day. There, Genentech's research chief, Aviv Regev, framed the company's direction as what she called AI independence. In her words, you have to own the learnings and the improvements that AI can develop.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis is simple. This week, the human behind the robot stopped being an engineering choice and became a priced input. California now mandates that human as a regulated operating cost for robotaxis. And a new humanoid startup is selling that same human as the product.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's two loudest stories in orbit are compute in space and a weaponized Golden Dome. Both are running ahead of what would make them real. For compute, that's flight-proven hardware. For Golden Dome, it's appropriated money.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline this week is that bank examiners have gone inside the private-credit plumbing itself. Semafor reported Monday that Fed examiners have been running on-site reviews at four major banks since the spring: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays, and Morgan Stanley.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's question is whether private-equity exits are actually unlocking. The short answer is yes, but narrowly. Preliminary PitchBook data show exit value surging on a handful of large sales, while the number of exits rose only modestly.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: DeepSeek is finalizing a funding round of at least eighty billion yuan, roughly twelve billion dollars, and pairing it with a plan to run at least one hundred sixty thousand Huawei chips in a new Inner Mongolia data center.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 7, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Nothing resolved cleanly overnight, but two calls come due this week, and several moved.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: All week we've treated the cheap, open layer of this market as China's story. In the space of about 48 hours, two Western labs stepped onto it.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Wednesday's session, because it said something the headline didn't. Oil and yields both rebounded. The S&P 500 slipped just 0.22 percent, a rounding error a day after its record close. The Russell 2000 fell 1.31 percent, roughly six times as hard.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with that test. Yesterday we said a daily close above $86,000 would show whether the long-term-holder and ETF breakeven band was acting as a floor or a ceiling. Bitcoin answered the other way. Shortly after midnight UTC on October 7th, it dropped below $84,000.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: The theme today is the gap between declaration and enforcement. You can see it on the water in the Strait of Hormuz. You can see it in a sanctions bill sitting on the president's desk. And you can see it inside the federal agency that's supposed to make sure America's biggest power grid has enough supply.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday the memory makers were asking for higher prices. Today one of them booked the profit. In logic manufacturing, though, the leverage still sits with whoever brings the capital, not with the foundry. That split is today's spine.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Over the last week, this beat has been about who controls agents and who pays for them. Today the answer itself changes shape, and the cheapest tier of the market gets a lot cheaper.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This week showed both sides of a single trade. One side is the cost of running enterprise software yourself. The other is how hard vendors are now pushing to run it for you, with as little friction as possible.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's money in AI drug discovery is going to biological data and wet-lab validation, not to models. Three stories make that case, and a fourth tells you who gets paid regardless of which model wins.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This week, the people setting the terms for embodied AI weren't the labs. They were lenders and a government. Credit funds just put a price on robotaxi risk. And China's magnet export lever comes back into play in about a month. Let's take those in order.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: On October 2nd we asked a simple question on this show. Is Washington going to be a brake on SpaceX's orbital ambitions, or an accelerant? This week gave us the answer.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thread is one firm standing on both sides of the valuation problem. Apollo is offering investors more frequent marks on its loans. In the same week, it is in talks to hold some of the hardest-to-mark exposures private credit has yet been asked to take on.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Exits aren't waiting for the window to reopen anymore. They're being built directly into the deal structure. A strategic buyer locks in a purchase right at entry. A general partner sells an asset to a vehicle it also controls.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: private credit is being asked to become the balance sheet behind OpenAI's compute bill, as Broadcom arranges more than fifty billion dollars in financing for the custom chip it's building with OpenAI.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard, because two calls resolved, and both landed.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: All week, the capability claims from the frontier labs have been vendor-reported, and token prices have kept falling. Google counted its own wins for Gemini 4 Argon, thirteen of eighteen benchmarks. Anthropic reported its own computer-use numbers for Haiku. Mistral published its own cyber scores for Large Four.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the session itself. On Thursday the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4 percent, its worst day in about seven weeks, per Bloomberg. The S&P 500 slipped just half a percent. Chip stocks took the real hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 3.4 percent. Oracle dropped more than 5 percent, again per Bloomberg.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: We start with a number we've been waiting for. Yesterday we said trackers pointed to an October 7th ETF outflow, but we declined to air a figure because none came with a source we could verify. Now one does.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's theme is easy to state and hard to trade around. Scarcity across the chip supply chain is now priced in. The open question is no longer how much gets shipped. It is who sets the price, and for how long.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday's story on this beat was about an answer changing shape inside a chat window. Today it's about AI moving into other people's software, and getting priced like a component rather than a product.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with OpenAI, because it just changed its own role in enterprise software. At its DevDay event at the end of September, OpenAI launched what it calls Marketplace. The launch roster has thirty-two partner vendors, spanning cybersecurity, customer experience, developer tools, legal tech and creative software.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Bloomberg reported on October 8th that Isomorphic Labs, the Alphabet drug-design spinout, is in early talks to raise new capital. Bloomberg's headline puts the target valuation at "at least $40 billion." Its sources put the range at forty to fifty billion dollars.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Three times this week, on Monday, Wednesday, and yesterday, this desk told you it found no fresh evidence from the robot-brain layer. That's the model layer that is supposed to turn humanoids and manipulators from demos into deployed labor. This week that silence broke.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline this week isn't that money is fleeing private credit. It's that money is re-sorting. And the newest place it's going is leverage stacked on top of private marks, right as supervisors start asking hard questions about exactly that layer.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: The question this week is who actually sets the price when a sponsor sells, because too much recent liquidity has been priced by insiders. That means continuation vehicles, co-sponsors, and counterparties with pre-negotiated purchase rights. This week gives us two genuinely arm's-length answers.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: a Financial Times report put OpenAI's annualized revenue near fifty billion dollars, about twenty billion below the figure that circulated last month, and the AI trade got marked to that number.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 9, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Nothing resolved cleanly overnight. One call is all but settled, and one I have to own.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: All week, the cheap end of the model stack has been under pressure from open weights and price cuts. Today, venture money backed a different kind of challenger, one that isn't even trying to be a general-purpose language model.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Two tests cleared this week, and the market is reading them very differently. The bond market's biggest test just passed. Underneath it, the oil story changed from a priced risk into barrels that are measurably missing. Let's take them in order.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday we told you to watch one level: whether bitcoin held eighty-three thousand dollars, a floor that had stood since late September. It didn't hold. Bitcoin printed eighty thousand, three hundred fifty dollars on Bitstamp, its lowest level since September 18th. That changes the job the level does.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's theme: both capitals are holding their hardest levers in reserve rather than pulling them. Meanwhile the one input neither side can negotiate, physical power, still runs on its own slow clock.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: This week the answer became an application. Two of the leading assistants decided that a chat response shouldn't just be text anymore. It should be a small piece of software. The open question is how that generated software earns trust. One answer is to make it disposable and inline.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Wall Street has decided that AI is an enabler for software, not a disruptor. This week's operating evidence says the real gates sit somewhere a stock price can't reach. The first is whether customers actually switch on the AI inside their own orgs. The second is whether data centers can get enough power to run it.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: The theme today is that the evidence bar in AI drug design is rising, from logos on a press release to falsifiable preclinical numbers. But both of today's developments stop at the same wall. They validate starting points, not drugs.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Golden Dome, because it answers a question we've been asking all week. On Wednesday we asked whether the money behind Golden Dome's awards actually exists. The Congressional Budget Office has now told Congress how much money a system meeting the president's executive order would actually need.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: the oil shock has turned from a priced risk into measurably missing barrels, just days before a CPI print that could validate the Fed's hawks.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 10, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Two calls landed this week. One looks like a miss, and one rested on a premise I got wrong.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Elon Musk. Nine to Five Mac reports that as of October 7th, Grok Bot runs Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 for its hardest tasks. Grok Bot is the consumer AI app from SpaceXAI, Musk's merged SpaceX and xAI entity. For disclosure, Anthropic makes the model behind this show.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the frame for today. The Fed hike did not disappear this week. It moved to December. Meanwhile, a near two-trillion-dollar deficit and a wave of AI borrowing are leaning on the same duration buyers. The bond market is pricing a higher-for-longer regime that equity volatility still refuses to price.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: A year ago this weekend, Bitcoin had its worst afternoon on record. Last October, days after a record high, Bitcoin fell from about $122,000 to $105,000, most of it within minutes. Roughly $19 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated across crypto markets.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thread running through today's news. Washington is allocating the cost of scarce energy by legal carve-out rather than letting markets clear it. Abroad, it is licensing Russian diesel back into world trade to protect the pump, even as Kyiv vows to keep burning the refineries that make that diesel.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: This week on this beat, we've covered the answer and the price: what the models say, and what they cost. Today's question is different. Who owns the agent that actually does the work?

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the lead, and a disclosure first. Anthropic makes the model behind this show, so weigh what follows accordingly. The Information reports that Anthropic cuts off an enterprise customer's discounted pricing the moment that customer exhausts its contracted token allotment.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Three times last week, this desk told you it had no fresh evidence from the robot-brain layer. That's the models, not the metal. On Friday the silence broke, but only with a CEO hire and some term sheets. Today it breaks properly, because the labs' own performance numbers are on the table.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the lead. On Thursday we told you the FCC had waived the requirement that a satellite operator lease spectrum from a terrestrial carrier before selling direct-to-device service. The same FCC action cleared SpaceX to launch up to fifteen thousand direct-to-device satellites.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Private credit's listed layer has gone from rationing liquidity to putting itself up for sale. On Friday, this desk argued that if stress was going to transmit anywhere first, it would show up as wider discounts in listed BDC shares, not as fresh gates in the semi-liquid retail funds.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Over the past week, this show has tracked a pattern of insider-priced liquidity. We've seen pre-sold exits, co-sponsor buyouts, and continuation-vehicle pricing that lands suspiciously close to the sponsor's own mark. This week's reporting adds a new wrinkle. It's not just the price. It's the carry.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: SpaceX reportedly agreed to buy roughly eight billion dollars of low-band spectrum, and T-Mobile and AT&T shares fell between seven and eleven percent intraday on a carrier threat whose satellites aren't built yet.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 11, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. One call resolved cleanly, and two moved on today's reads.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this desk has watched cyber and safety turn into the stage where the labs compete, rather than the fine print beneath it. Today that shift sharpens. One lab disclosed a failure inside its own training process. Another turned access to its most dangerous capability into a tiered product.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Cash markets were closed for the weekend, so the freshest information is not a price. It is a flow dataset, and it confirms a call this desk made last week. The speculative sleeve is de-risking, and the full-week numbers say it is happening everywhere at once.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Last week's institutional retreat from crypto turned out to be broader than it first looked. But a good chunk of what broadened it is plumbing, not conviction. Separating the two is today's job.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Three stories this week share the same shape. A state holds a formal lever over something scarce: airwaves, advanced chips, Russian energy. An actor then tries to route around that lever or outbid it. In each case, the outcome is decided by the approval or the enforcement, not the announcement.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: The thesis today: scarcity pricing keeps spreading through the chip stack. And the industry is splitting into two camps. There are companies that can hold their price, and companies that need someone else's balance sheet to survive long enough to compete. A word of warning up front. It's a light news week.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: One disclosure before we start, because it bears directly on the lead story: Anthropic makes the model behind this show. Here's today's thesis. Microsoft is buying less Claude for its own staff while selling more of it to customers, and that tells you where leverage in enterprise AI is moving.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the lead. Iambic Therapeutics, the Nvidia-backed AI-native drug designer, filed an amended S-1 on October 8th to list on Nasdaq under the ticker IAM. At the top of its price range, the deal would value Iambic at up to about 800 million dollars.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's shift in physical AI is about who pays. Two of the Pentagon's most important autonomy vendors, Anduril and Shield AI, put their own capital in alongside the government's. In Anduril's case, the private money is the larger share. Defense is now where autonomy vendors co-finance production at prime scale.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's today's thread. SpaceX is buying up scarce inputs, first spectrum and now possibly compute, and last week the market marked down nearly everyone standing near it. But the sharpest piece of that story, what it means for AST SpaceMobile, is more contested than Friday's tape suggested.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis in two sentences. The fight over whether private credit's marks mean anything now has a courtroom track, not just a supervisory one. And the same discretion that sets a mark also decides what counts as a default.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: the market has delivered its first full verdict on SpaceX's spectrum deal with Grain Management, hammering the carriers and AST SpaceMobile, but that verdict prices an FCC approval that hasn't happened, and the sell side is already disputing the read on AST.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — October 12, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Nothing resolved over the weekend. One call moved, and several come due this week.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thread running through today's developments. Capability parity is getting cheap to claim, so the labs are pulling their best models into products they alone own and bill. At the same time, the commercial scoreboard everyone uses to judge who's winning just turned out to be softer than priced.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the frame. Last week, mainstream investors started repositioning for a higher-for-longer rate world. Money moved into bonds, and out of equities and crypto. Today's bank earnings and tomorrow's CPI are the first live tests of that move.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis up front. Bitcoin just took its second long squeeze in three days, and it fell last week while gold rose. On that evidence, the market is pricing bitcoin as levered risk beta, not as digital gold.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Three developments moved the base layer of the AI buildout. A federal regulator closed a fast lane for data-center power in America's largest grid. A nuclear fuel market set a record its own equities don't seem to believe. And Moscow opened a diesel tap that Washington had just licensed.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. Last week the chip equity market and the memory contract market handed down opposite verdicts on whether AI demand actually lasts. This week's prints from ASML and TSMC start to settle which one had it right.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: The model headlines this week are mostly reruns on this beat. The real movement is in the plumbing underneath the models. Two questions sit there: what an AI agent is allowed to touch, and who gets to decide which model it runs. Three items this week answer them in three different directions, and that's today's spine.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's today's thesis. Security demand has just shown up in reseller channel data, but the gains are concentrating in a few platforms. Those same platforms are becoming the trusted distribution channel for enterprise AI. That's concentration, not a rising tide.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Here's the thesis for today. The AI buildout is outgrowing bank balance sheets, and banks are now trying to hand that risk to non-banks just as the market marks the anchor tenant's credit down.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has asked one question. Who, if anyone, is pricing private equity at arm's length? The secondaries market has now answered, and the answer splits by asset quality.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — October 13, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: four banks have spent more than six months unable to offload thirty-eight billion dollars of construction debt tied to a single Oracle-leased data-center project, because AI-linked exposure is bumping against their own internal limits.
